documents.title: New Patient Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32F software engineer, works remotely, establishing care. Prior PCP retired; records reviewed.

No complaints. Sleeps ok, walks most days, some yoga.

PMH: none.
PSH: tonsillectomy age 8, third molars removed age 21.
Gyn: menarche 11, G0, regular cycles on OCP. Sees her own gynecologist; last Pap/HPV 5/2022 negative.
Meds: norgestimate 0.25 / EE 35 mcg daily (gyn prescribes), vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs. Single.
FH: mother - breast cancer at 42, then ovarian cancer at 51. Maternal aunt breast cancer at 39. Maternal grandmother breast cancer at 44. Father has hypertension. Family is of Eastern European Jewish background.

Exam: well appearing. HEENT normal, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts symmetric, no masses, skin or nipple changes; no axillary or supraclavicular nodes. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin fair, burns easily (Fitzpatrick II by her description), no lesions of concern on a quick look at arms, face, back. No edema.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance - CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH; HIV and hep C once. Tdap today (last one was in high school). Cervical screening per her gyn, next due 2027.
2. Family history of breast and ovarian cancer - three affected relatives on mom's side, two diagnosed before 45, plus ovarian. This easily meets criteria for genetic counseling and BRCA testing, and her ancestry adds to it. Talked through what a positive result would mean for screening. She has thought about it before and wants to hold off for now; she wants to look into insurance implications first. Will revisit at next physical. Encouraged breast self-awareness, report any change.
3. Contraception - continue OCP through gyn.
4. Fair skin - sunscreen, hats; low threshold for a skin check if anything changes.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Lump
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi Doctor, I felt a hard lump in my right breast in the shower this week, toward the armpit side. It doesn't hurt. I called my gynecologist and they can see me Monday the 9th and said they would try to get imaging the same day. Should I also come in? Given my mom's history I'm pretty anxious.

documents.title: RE: Lump
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me. Keeping the Monday visit with your gynecologist is the right move, especially if they can get the mammogram and ultrasound done that day - that is the fastest path. You don't need a separate visit here first. Please ask them to send me their note and the imaging, and message me once you hear anything. If they can't get imaging scheduled quickly, let me know and I will order it.

conditions.label: Unspecified lump in the right breast, upper outer quadrant

reports.text:
Outside breast imaging center. Indication: palpable right breast mass, upper outer quadrant, found on self-exam. Family history of breast cancer. No prior mammograms for comparison.
Technique: bilateral diagnostic digital mammography with tomosynthesis; spot compression views of the right breast at the palpable marker.
Findings: The breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses. Underlying the palpable marker in the right upper outer quadrant there is an irregular mass with indistinct margins. No associated calcifications or architectural distortion elsewhere. Left breast without suspicious mass, calcifications or distortion. No skin thickening.
reports.conclusion: Right breast upper outer quadrant irregular mass corresponding to the palpable finding, suspicious. BI-RADS 4. Ultrasound performed same day, see separate report; tissue sampling recommended.

reports.text:
Outside breast imaging center. Targeted right breast and right axillary ultrasound.
Findings: At 10 o'clock, 6 cm from the nipple, at the palpable site, there is an irregular hypoechoic mass measuring 2.3 x 1.8 x 1.6 cm, not parallel to the skin. No internal vascularity of note. No skin thickening. The right axilla shows normal-appearing lymph nodes with preserved fatty hila.
reports.conclusion: Irregular hypoechoic mass right breast 10 o'clock, 2.3 cm, corresponding to the mammographic finding. BI-RADS 4. Ultrasound-guided core biopsy recommended and scheduled.

documents.title: Gynecology consult: right breast mass
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside gynecology practice
Date of service: 12/09/2024
Patient: Deborah Lipschitz, DOB 10/21/1990

Reason: palpable mass right breast.

34-year-old G0, menarche at 11, presents after noticing a firm lump in the upper outer right breast while showering last week. Asymptomatic otherwise - no pain, no nipple discharge, no skin change.

Medications: norgestimate/ethinyl estradiol 0.25 mg/35 mcg daily; cholecalciferol 2000 IU daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Surgical history: tonsillectomy (age 8), wisdom tooth extraction (age 21).
Family history: mother with breast cancer at 42 and ovarian cancer at 51; maternal aunt breast cancer at 39; maternal grandmother breast cancer at 44. Father hypertension.
Social: nonsmoker, no alcohol.

Exam: right breast UOQ with a firm, fixed 2.5 cm mass. Overlying skin normal, no retraction, no nipple discharge on expression. Left breast normal. No axillary, supraclavicular or cervical adenopathy. Remainder of exam unremarkable.

Imaging today: diagnostic mammogram shows a suspicious irregular mass at the palpable site; same-day ultrasound confirms a 2.3 cm irregular mass at 10 o'clock, BI-RADS 4. Reports attached.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Right breast mass, suspicious on imaging - ultrasound-guided core biopsy booked for 12/13.
2. Strong maternal history of breast and ovarian cancer and Jewish ancestry - hereditary cancer panel sent today after pre-test counseling; results in about 3-4 weeks. Will refer to genetic counseling for results.
3. Contraception - continue current pill for now pending results.
Copy to primary care physician.

conditions.label: Unspecified lump in the right breast, upper outer quadrant
Benign neoplasm of right breast
conditions.note: fibroadenoma, 10 o'clock, core biopsy 12/13/2024, clip placed

reports.text:
Outside pathology laboratory.
Specimen: right breast, 10 o'clock, ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy (14-gauge, 4 cores). Post-biopsy clip placed; post-procedure mammogram confirms clip at the biopsy site.
Gross: four tan-white cores, 1.2 to 1.6 cm, entirely submitted.
Microscopic: biphasic lesion with proliferating stroma of low cellularity and compressed ducts lined by benign epithelium with a myoepithelial layer. No stromal overgrowth or atypia. No atypical ductal hyperplasia, in situ or invasive carcinoma identified.
Radiology-pathology correlation (breast imaging): benign concordant result.
reports.conclusion: Right breast 10 o'clock core biopsy: fibroadenoma. Negative for atypia and malignancy. Concordant; follow-up ultrasound of the right breast in 6 months.

procedures.procedure: Core needle biopsy of breast using imaging guidance

documents.title: Your biopsy

Your genetic test is still out; once it is back, let's meet to talk about what it means for you either way.

documents.title: Genetic counseling letter: hereditary cancer panel
documents.author: genetic counseling
documents.body:
Outside cancer genetics service
Date of result disclosure: 01/07/2025
Re: Deborah Lipschitz, DOB 10/21/1990
Ordering clinician: her gynecologist; copy to primary care.

Ms. Lipschitz had a multigene hereditary cancer panel sent on 12/09/2024 in the setting of a right breast mass (since shown to be a fibroadenoma) and a significant maternal history: mother with breast cancer at 42 and ovarian cancer at 51, maternal aunt with breast cancer at 39, maternal grandmother with breast cancer at 44. Jewish ancestry.

Result (reported 01/06/2025): heterozygous pathogenic variant in BRCA1. No other pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were found.

Interpretation: this confirms hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome. Women with a BRCA1 pathogenic variant have a substantially increased lifetime risk of breast cancer and of ovarian/fallopian tube cancer compared with the general population.

We discussed by video for about an hour:
- Breast: high-risk surveillance with yearly MRI and yearly mammogram; risk-reducing mastectomy as an option.
- Ovarian: risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy is the recommended approach, generally between 35 and 40 or when childbearing is complete. Screening ultrasound and CA-125 are not reliable substitutes.
- Family: each first-degree relative has a 50% chance of carrying the variant. Family letter provided; whether to share it is her choice.
- Insurance and GINA protections reviewed.
We recommend referral to a high-risk breast program. She was given the full lab report.
Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: BRCA1 pathogenic variant, high-risk breast surveillance and risk-reduction planning

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34F here to go over her genetics result with me. Panel from 12/9: BRCA1 pathogenic variant, nothing else. Genetic counselor letter reviewed together.

She is processing it; not surprised given her mom. Somewhat regrets waiting, I told her that the timing changed nothing that matters now. No new breast symptoms. The right breast fibroadenoma has not changed in size to her touch.

Meds: OCP, vitamin D3. NKDA.
BP and weight as charted. Breasts: R UOQ firm area at the healed biopsy site, as before; no new mass, no nodes.

A/P:
1. Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome (BRCA1) - added to problem list. Referral to high-risk breast program for MRI/mammogram surveillance and a discussion of risk-reducing options. Ovarian risk reduction (salpingo-oophorectomy) explained in broad strokes; she is single, does not know yet about children, and is not ready to think about surgery. The OCP actually lowers ovarian risk; fine to continue, will defer to the high-risk team.
2. Fibroadenoma R breast - 6 mo US due June, the high-risk program can coordinate with MRI.
3. Offered behavioral health support if the news weighs on her; she will reach out if she wants it.
Follow up at physical or sooner.

documents.title: High-risk breast program consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside cancer center, High-Risk Breast Program
Visit date: 02/18/2025
Referred by: primary care physician

Dear Doctor,
Thank you for referring Ms. Lipschitz, a 34-year-old woman with a newly identified BRCA1 pathogenic variant. In December she presented with a palpable right breast mass at 10 o'clock, 2.3 cm on ultrasound and BI-RADS 4; core biopsy showed fibroadenoma, concordant. Menarche 11, nulliparous, on a combined oral contraceptive. Family history as documented by genetics (mother breast 42 and ovarian 51; maternal aunt breast 39; maternal grandmother breast 44). No prior chest radiation.
Medications: norgestimate/ethinyl estradiol daily; vitamin D3 2000 IU. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: breasts symmetric; healed biopsy site right upper outer quadrant with a firm area consistent with the known fibroadenoma. No other masses, skin or nipple changes. No axillary or supraclavicular nodes.

Assessment and recommendations:
1. BRCA1 carrier - high-risk surveillance: contrast breast MRI yearly and mammogram yearly, staggered six months apart. First MRI in June together with the planned 6-month right breast ultrasound; mammogram in December. Clinical breast exam here every 6 to 12 months.
2. Risk-reducing bilateral mastectomy reviewed in detail, including reconstruction. She does not wish to pursue it at present, which is a reasonable choice with MRI surveillance; we will revisit yearly.
3. Risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy recommended between ages 35 and 40, once her plans about childbearing are clearer. We will refer to gynecologic oncology whenever she is ready to discuss timing.
4. The oral contraceptive may be continued.
Return in 6 months after her MRI.

reports.study: MRI breast, bilateral, with and without contrast
reports.text:
Outside cancer center imaging. Indication: BRCA1 carrier, high-risk screening, baseline. Known fibroadenoma right breast.
Technique: bilateral breast MRI before and after IV gadolinium, multiplanar, with subtraction and kinetic analysis.
Findings: Heterogeneous fibroglandular tissue, mild background parenchymal enhancement. Right breast 10 o'clock: oval circumscribed mass with dark internal septations corresponding to the biopsy-proven fibroadenoma, with associated clip artifact; size unchanged from ultrasound. No suspicious masses or non-mass enhancement in either breast. No axillary or internal mammary adenopathy. Visualized chest wall unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Biopsy-proven fibroadenoma right breast, unchanged. No MRI evidence of malignancy. BI-RADS 2, benign. Continue high-risk surveillance: mammogram in 6 months, MRI in 12 months.

reports.text:
Outside cancer center imaging. Targeted right breast ultrasound, 6-month follow-up of biopsied fibroadenoma at 10 o'clock.
Findings: hypoechoic mass at the biopsy site with echogenic clip, size unchanged from December 2024. No new solid or cystic lesions in the scanned area. Normal right axillary nodes.
reports.conclusion: Stable biopsy-proven fibroadenoma. BI-RADS 2. No further dedicated ultrasound follow-up needed; continue surveillance imaging.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
35F with BRCA1 and fair skin here for a mole on the upper back. Present for many years; over the last few months she thinks it has grown and darkened, edge looks irregular in her photos. No pain, itch or bleeding. Burns easily; gets sun on her back at the beach on vacations.

documents.title: Dermatology consultation and excisional biopsy
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group
Date of visit: 06/15/2026
Referring: primary care physician

HPI: 35-year-old woman, BRCA1 carrier (worked up after a breast mass in late 2024, benign fibroadenoma), referred for a longstanding mole on the upper back that she feels has changed in look over recent months. Denies pain or pruritus.

PMH: hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome (BRCA1); right breast fibroadenoma. Fitzpatrick skin type II.
PSH: tonsillectomy (8), wisdom teeth (21), breast core biopsy 2024.
Meds: ethinyl estradiol/norgestimate daily; cholecalciferol 2000 IU daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father has had melanoma. Maternal breast and ovarian cancers as documented.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, software engineer.

Exam (full skin exam): Upper back - 1 cm pigmented lesion, asymmetric, irregular borders, mixed brown and black. She reports this area gets sun on vacations. Dermoscopy: irregular streaks at the periphery and a blue-white veil. No palpable cervical, axillary or inguinal lymphadenopathy. Remainder of the skin exam unremarkable; scattered benign-appearing freckles and nevi.

Assessment: atypical pigmented lesion of the upper back, highly concerning for melanoma.

Procedure today: excisional biopsy with 2 mm margins, elliptical, closed in layers, after informed consent and local lidocaine with epinephrine. Specimen to dermatopathology. Tolerated well. Wound care reviewed.

Plan: pathology in about 1 week; we will call her. Suture removal in 2 weeks.

conditions.label: Malignant melanoma of other part of trunk
conditions.note: nodular melanoma, upper back, Breslow 1.6 mm, nonulcerated, pT2a

reports.text:
Outside dermatopathology.
Specimen: skin, upper back, excisional biopsy.
Gross: skin ellipse 1.6 x 0.9 cm, excised to a depth of 0.6 cm, with a central 1.0 cm variegated pigmented lesion; inked and serially sectioned, entirely submitted.
Microscopic: Invasive melanoma, nodular type.
- Breslow thickness: 1.6 mm
- Ulceration: absent
- Dermal mitotic rate: 3 per mm2
- Microsatellites: not identified
- Lymphovascular invasion: not identified
- Perineural invasion: not identified
- Regression: not identified
- Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes: non-brisk
- Margins: peripheral and deep margins free of melanoma; closest peripheral margin 1.5 mm.
Pathologic stage (AJCC 8th edition): pT2a.
reports.conclusion: Skin, upper back, excision: invasive nodular melanoma, Breslow 1.6 mm, nonulcerated, mitoses 3/mm2, margins negative (narrow). pT2a. Wide local excision and sentinel lymph node evaluation advised.

documents.title: Dermatopathology and dermatology note
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group - result note 06/19/2026
Pathology reviewed with the patient by phone today. Excisional biopsy of the upper back shows nodular melanoma, 1.6 mm, without ulceration (pT2a). Discussed that the standard next step is wider excision with sentinel lymph node biopsy. Referred to surgical oncology; appointment requested within 2 weeks. She will continue full skin exams with us every 3 months after surgery.
Allergies: NKDA.
Copy: primary care.

documents.title: Call after skin pathology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called her after receiving the derm pathology. She had heard from derm Friday. Melanoma on the back, 1.6 mm, not ulcerated. Surgical oncology visit is set for 7/8 with surgery planned that day if the node mapping is arranged. She is upset but organized; she watched her mother go through cancer care and knows how to ask questions. Answered questions: this is separate from the BRCA1 result as far as we know, and her breast surveillance stays on schedule. She will keep her July physical; told her to message any time before then.

events.reason: surgical oncology operative and pathology reports

reports.text:
Outside hospital pathology.
A. Skin and subcutaneous tissue, upper back, wide local excision: ellipse 7.2 x 4.4 cm, depth to fascia, with a healing scar centrally. No residual melanoma. Margins free.
B. Lymph node, right axillary sentinel #1 (hot, blue): one lymph node, negative for metastatic melanoma (0/1) on H&E and immunohistochemistry (SOX10, Melan-A).
C. Lymph node, right axillary sentinel #2 (hot): one lymph node, negative for metastatic melanoma (0/1) on H&E and immunohistochemistry.
Final pathologic stage with prior biopsy: pT2a pN0 (0/2 sentinel nodes).
reports.conclusion: No residual melanoma, margins clear. Two right axillary sentinel lymph nodes negative (0/2). pT2a N0 - stage IB.

documents.title: Surgical oncology operative note and pathology
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Outside surgical oncology
Date of surgery: 07/08/2026
Preoperative diagnosis: melanoma of the upper back, Breslow 1.6 mm, nonulcerated (pT2a)
Procedure: wide local excision upper back with 2 cm margins, primary closure; preoperative lymphoscintigraphy and sentinel lymph node biopsy, right axilla.
Anesthesia: general. EBL minimal. No complications.
Lymphoscintigraphy showed drainage to the right axilla only. Two sentinel nodes removed (one hot and blue, one hot); no further hot nodes after removal.
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: oral contraceptive, vitamin D3.
Discharged home same day.

Addendum 07/13/2026: final pathology - no residual melanoma, clear margins; both sentinel nodes negative. Stage IB (pT2a N0 M0). No adjuvant systemic therapy is indicated. Surveillance: skin and lymph node examination every 3 to 6 months, alternating between dermatology and our clinic, for the first years. Routine cross-sectional imaging is not indicated in the absence of symptoms. Post-op visit 07/28.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
35F annual, two weeks out from wide excision and sentinel node biopsy for melanoma of the upper back.

Interval: derm saw a changing mole 6/15 and excised it - nodular melanoma, Breslow 1.6 mm, no ulceration. Surgical oncology 7/8: WLE with 2 cm margins, 2 R axillary sentinel nodes, all negative, no residual tumor. Stage IB, no further treatment, surveillance every 3-6 months alternating derm and surg onc. Breast MRI 6/10 BI-RADS 2.

Recovering well. Back incision a little tight when she reaches overhead; armpit sore the first week, now fine. No arm swelling. Little pain after the first few days. Mood: shaken but steady, sleeping ok, back at work full time. Tells me her father had a melanoma removed years ago; she had not known to mention it.

Meds: norgestimate/EE daily, D3 2000 units. NKDA.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: well, NAD. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Upper back: long horizontal incision healing well, edges together, no erythema, drainage or fluid collection. Right axilla: small healed incision, no seroma, no palpable nodes. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes. Breasts deferred to high-risk program (seen with MRI in June). Abdomen benign. No arm edema.

A/P:
1. Melanoma upper back, stage IB, s/p WLE/SLNB - healing well. Follow-up per derm and surg onc. Daily sunscreen, protective clothing, monthly self skin checks; suggested mirror or phone photos for her back.
2. Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome (BRCA1) - surveillance up to date, mammogram due December. She turns 36 in October; we talked again about the 35-40 window for salpingo-oophorectomy. She would like the gyn onc conversation this fall once she is past the surgery recovery; we will place it at her fall visit.
3. Family history - father's melanoma added.
4. Fibroadenoma R breast - stable on imaging.
5. Preventive: PHQ-2 1, not depressed, coping. CBC and CMP today as a baseline after surgery. Pap per gyn 2027. Flu/COVID at the October visit.
RTC October.

Date of visit: 07/28/2026

Ms. Lipschitz returns 3 weeks after wide local excision of her upper back melanoma and right axillary sentinel lymph node biopsy. Final pathology was reviewed again with her: no residual disease, 0/2 nodes, stage IB.
She is doing well with minimal discomfort.
Exam: back incision well healed, no seroma. Axillary incision healed. No palpable adenopathy. No lymphedema.
Allergies: NKDA.
Plan unchanged: skin and nodal exams every 3 to 6 months alternating with dermatology; next here in 6 months. Activity without restriction. Sun protection reinforced.
